item.title: Le Garage Moderne: OASIS International Artist Residencies 2026 (Bordeaux)
item.description:
Organisation: Le Garage Moderne (European OASIS project)

Location: Bacalan district, Bordeaux, France. Le Garage Moderne is a non-profit car garage and bicycle workshop, a canteen serving sponsored meals, and a cultural venue housing 11 permanent artists, makers and craftswomen, recently returned to its 19th-century building after a two-and-a-half-year renovation.

Award: Five grants. Each artist receives a fee of EUR 1,300 gross (taxes may apply depending on legal status), up to EUR 600 for production expenses such as raw materials, technical services or special tools, a lump-sum travel grant scaled to distance with top-ups for green travel options, a per diem of EUR 45 per day, and accommodation in a self-catering hotel. Access to the shared tools and spaces of Le Garage Moderne is included, subject to the association's regulations. No application fee.

Duration: Two weeks on site. Five overlapping two-week slots, and applicants may choose one or more: 9 to 22 November, 16 to 29 November, 23 November to 6 December, 30 November to 13 December, and 7 to 20 December 2026. Deadline 1 September 2026; pre-selection interviews 15 September; final selection announced 1 October 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Second year of Le Garage Moderne's residency cycle within the European OASIS project, offering five grants to international artists for two-week stays in Bordeaux. THE SITE IS THE POINT. Le Garage Moderne is a working non-profit car and bicycle workshop with a neighbourhood canteen and a versatile venue for performing arts, concerts and community gatherings, all at once a productive space, a public space and a community-driven common. Having just moved back into its 19th-century building after a long renovation, the team describes machines and workbenches back in place and a brand-new playground, and invites residents to take over the space and explore its physical and social possibilities. They ask for SITE-SPECIFIC PROPOSALS that play with the verticality, the scale of the space, the community and what they call the hive-like vibe of the venue, where everyone runs around, shouts, gets their hands dirty and learns in the process. DISCIPLINES: any, explicitly including design, visual art, performing arts, film, small-scale architecture, emergency architecture, craft-making, street furniture, sound, and interdisciplinary or community-based practices. Proposals combining artistic creation with the spatial and the social are especially encouraged, and the organisers say plainly that they want to be surprised. WHAT IS EXPECTED: openness to exchange and collaboration with the 11 permanent residents and with 3 local artists recruited through a separate OASIS call; participation in 2 days of masterclass open to members and community, where you describe and share your practice, technique and working context with fellow OASIS residents, local artists, members and staff; and a public outcome, which need not be a large event but must be something the public can experience. RIGHTS: work produced during the residency remains the artist's property, but documentation of it is made by Le Garage Moderne and will be publicised by them for three years after the residency. Note this is a different OASIS partner call from the OASis In the Park (Naples) and Disappearing Landscape (High Tatras) rounds under the same European project.

item.title: ITER 2026: International Touring and Environmental Responsibility Programme
item.description:
Organisation: Julie's Bicycle and in futurum, funded by Arts Council England, Arts Council Norway, Creative Scotland and the Danish Arts Foundation

Location: England, Scotland, Norway and Denmark. Seminars run online.

Award: The seminar programme is free to join. Groups of three or more participants can then apply for up to GBP 30,000 for collaborative projects, with funding applications open 6 November 2026 to 11 January 2027 and projects starting spring 2027. No application fee.

Duration: Seminars run weekly from 1 October to 10 December 2026, Tuesdays for Pathfinders and Thursdays for Changemakers, 10:00 to 12:00 UK time. Deadline to join 1 September 2026.

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

ITER is now in its fifth year and supports people in the performing arts to build environmentally responsible, inclusive and equitable ways of touring and collaborating internationally. It is initiated and financed by Arts Council England, Arts Council Norway, Creative Scotland and the Danish Arts Foundation, and designed and delivered by Julie's Bicycle and in futurum. Creative Scotland joined as a partner for 2026. TWO TRACKS, up to 60 places in total: PATHFINDERS, ten sessions introducing the principles of sustainable touring for people new to the subject; and CHANGEMAKERS, nine sessions for those further along, on leadership and systemic change. Seminars run weekly from 1 October to 10 December 2026, Pathfinders on Tuesdays and Changemakers on Thursdays, 10:00 to 12:00 UK time, alongside networking and a new alumni network. THE MONEY COMES IN PHASE TWO: after the seminars, groups of three or more participants can apply for up to GBP 30,000 to implement collaborative projects that cut environmental impacts and advance climate justice. Funding applications open 6 November 2026 and close 11 January 2027; awarded projects begin in spring 2027. ELIGIBILITY: based in England, Scotland, Norway or Denmark, working in dance, music or theatre. That covers music and theatre venues receiving touring work, festivals, orchestras, theatre companies, solo artists, performers and musicians, performing arts producers, and multidisciplinary arts organisations. Applications are made through the relevant national funder (Arts Council England open funds, Creative Scotland targeted funding, Arts Council Norway, Danish Arts Foundation). Questions go to environmentaltouring@artscouncil.org.uk.

item.title: Reflection (All Disciplines)
item.description:
Organisation: Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council)

Location: Collectives of at least two cultural practitioners; for international collaborations at least 50 percent must be from Switzerland.

Award: Maximum CHF 25,000 (cannot exceed 50 percent of total budget). No application fee.

Duration: Collective mediation project fostering critical reflection; deadlines twice yearly (1 March and 1 September).

Deadline: 01 Sep 2026

Reflection is a Pro Helvetia grant supporting collective mediation projects that use innovative formats to foster critical reflection on artistic practice and cultural transformation, across all supported disciplines (design, literature, music, performing arts, visual arts, and innovation and society). Open to collectives comprising at least two cultural practitioners (artists, creatives, cultural practitioners, or art educators); solo projects are excluded. ELIGIBILITY: requires a connection to Switzerland (Swiss citizenship, or permanent residency with regular artistic activity in Switzerland); not open to practitioners without a Swiss connection. For international collaborations, at least 50 percent of practitioners must be from Switzerland. AMOUNT: maximum CHF 25,000, and no more than 50 percent of the total budget. Deadlines twice a year: 1 March (23:59 CET) and 1 September (23:59 CEST). Apply via the Pro Helvetia portal.

item.title: National Gallery of Iceland: CUSP Artist Residency (Reykjavik 2027)
item.description:
Organisation: National Gallery of Iceland (Listasafn Islands), CUSP project

Location: Reykjavik, Iceland. Residency hosted by the National Gallery of Iceland.

Award: Accommodation and working space for the residency; travel and subsistence stipend; an artist fee for collaborating in the open-lab/masterclass; and, depending on the artist's request and museum means, hardware and software for the working space. No application fee.

Duration: Up to four weeks, taking place in early 2027, with exact dates arranged with the selected artist.

Deadline: 03 Sep 2026

The National Gallery of Iceland announces an artist residency open call under its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe's Culture grant. Artists working in complex media or emerging technologies (e.g. generative AI, custom sensors, sound, software-based, blockchain, physical and digital hybrid) are invited to apply. This is the first of four residency stays offered to different artists through the program, one in each of the participating countries (Iceland, Norway, Czechia, and Ukraine), followed by two micro residencies in the Netherlands and Iceland. The programme brings together artists working in time-based media with museum professionals, conservators, and technology specialists developing preservation and conservation methodologies to ensure the long-term endurance of artworks. The selected artist will meet with a preservation specialist or conservator specializing in time-based media art for an in-depth artist interview addressing the preservation needs of their medium, and will present their body of work and working methods publicly during an open-lab masterclass designed in collaboration with the museum. RESIDENCY: up to four weeks in early 2027 in Reykjavik, exact dates arranged with the selected artist. WHAT IS PROVIDED: accommodation and working space; a travel and subsistence stipend; an artist fee for the open lab/masterclass; and possibly hardware and software depending on the artist's request and museum means. ELIGIBILITY: international artists based outside Iceland; applicants must be residents of any of the 27 EU member states or of non-EU countries with association agreements (EFTA/EEA members, acceding countries, candidate countries, and European Neighbourhood Policy countries). APPLICATION: complete the application form with full name, country of residence, gender identity, contact information, an artistic statement (max 2500 characters), a motivation letter (max 2500 characters), a draft idea of the public workshop or masterclass (max 1000 characters), links to social media/professional websites, and a CV and portfolio upload (max 10MB each). DEADLINE: 3 September 2026 at 23:59 GMT. ABOUT CUSP: Creative Understanding, Saving and Preserving Time-Based Media Art is a transnational cooperation project co-funded by the EU's Creative Europe Culture grant, led by the National Gallery of Iceland with Nasjonalmuseet (Norway), LI-MA (Netherlands), Vasulka Kitchen (Czechia), and Mystetskyi Art Arsenal (Ukraine), focused on preserving and presenting time-based media art. Inquiries: cusp.residency.is [at] gmail.com.

item.title: Híbrides: Small Embodied Data - Call for Contributions (2nd Edition)
item.description:
Organisation: Axolot.cat collective and DARTS research group, Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC)

Location: Barcelona, Spain; UOC Poblenou campus and Convent de Sant Agustí. In-person attendance required.

Award: Oral presentations: €100 honorarium (invoice required). Performances: €400 honorarium (invoice required). No submission fee.

Duration: Festival runs 26-28 November 2026.

Deadline: 07 Sep 2026

Híbrides is a biennial of artistic research co-organised by the Axolot.cat collective and the DARTS (Design, Art, Technology and Society) research group at the UOC in Barcelona. The second edition, "Small Embodied Data," centres on the concept of classification -- approached through machine learning, data science, algorithmic systems, and questions of who designs classifiers, under what ethical codes, and to what end. The biennial brings classification into dialogue with its previous themes of Small Data (community-defined, intentional data collection and analysis) and Embodiment (bodily experience as a foundation of situated, sensory knowledge). Both academic and non-academic contributions are welcome. FORMATS ACCEPTED: Oral Presentations (20 minutes; artistic practice, artistic research, or academic research projects; may be video-recorded for a public archive and developed into short papers); Performances (20-30 minutes; must engage with the physical body, stage, and technology; complete works, including previously presented work; takes place in a multipurpose space with technical support). SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: online form with abstract (max 1,000 characters), professional biography (max 1,000 characters), and link to representative materials (3-5 images; video and technical rider required for performances). HONORARIA: oral presentations €100; performances €400; invoice required in both cases. Participants must follow the event's code of conduct. Event runs 26-28 November 2026 at UOC Poblenou campus and Convent de Sant Agustí, Barcelona. Deadline: 7 September 2026. Submit at https://hibrides.axolot.cat/opencall.html.

item.title: Studio ALTA Residence 2027: four residency open calls (Prague)
item.description:
Organisation: Studio ALTA

Location: Studio ALTA, Prague (Liben district), Czech Republic. Three of the four calls are open internationally; the Rest House call is reserved for supporting-profession arts workers active in the Czech independent sector.

Award: Residency fees paid to participants: Research House CZK 12,000 per project; Rest House CZK 6,000 per person; House in the Neighborhood CZK 30,000 per project; House of Sweat CZK 15,000 per project. All include workspace at Studio ALTA; the two production residencies add dramaturgic, production, technical and PR support. Free to apply.

Duration: Programme dependent: 5 to 10 days, at various points between February and November 2027

Deadline: 10 Sep 2026

Prague performance venue Studio ALTA announces four residency open calls for 2027, all with a single deadline of 10 September 2026. RESEARCH HOUSE (19 to 28 April 2027): a shared residential laboratory for three art projects or individual artists in the early stages of exploration and experimentation, or reopening an existing finished work (performance, installation, object, video) to transform it into another form such as a workshop, text or performance-lecture. Includes a 10-day residency, a fee of CZK 12,000 per project, shared studio, individual workspace and facilitated exchange meetings; the research output must be shared publicly as a work-in-progress in a form based on participants' needs. REST HOUSE (March to November 2027): a five-day residential spa for overloaded colleagues from the arts sector, with no required output or activities; restricted to people working in production, dramaturgy, curation, PR, technical and other supporting artistic professions in the Czech independent sector. Two guests are chosen by lottery (fee CZK 6,000 per person); the public draw is announced 16 September 2026. HOUSE IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD (9 to 18 August 2027): for one performative art project created with the local community and designed or adapted for public space in Liben and its surroundings; this year's call focuses on the 55+ target group. Includes a fee of CZK 30,000 per project, rehearsal and indoor facilities (primarily outdoor spaces), dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, connections to partner organisations, and 7 days of intensive production and technical support in the final phase. A public premiere or work-in-progress in public space at the end of the residency is required. HOUSE OF SWEAT (1 to 10 February 2027): for one performative art project designed or adapted for the specific environment of the Studio ALTA sauna and its immediate surroundings, seeking new ways of working with intimate space, proximity to the audience and non-traditional formats. Includes a fee of CZK 15,000 per project, a 10-day residency, sauna and rehearsal spaces, dramaturgic, production, technical and PR consultation, and 2 days of intensive final-phase support; a public work-in-progress or premiere in the sauna within the 9 to 12 February 2027 programme block is required. Projects at any stage of development can apply to the production calls, and selected projects may be included in Studio ALTA's year-round programme. TIMELINE: deadline 10 September 2026; results 3 weeks after the deadline (30 September 2026); a Q&A Zoom call takes place 10 August 2026 at 3:00 PM. Apply via the registration forms on the call page.

item.title: Martin Roth-Initiative: Temporary Relocation for Artists and Cultural Actors at Risk (Programme Line 1, 2026 call)
item.description:
Organisation: Martin Roth-Initiative (Goethe-Institut and ifa, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office)

Location: Germany (relocation to a German host organisation). Open to artists and cultural actors worldwide, with exclusions.

Award: Monthly scholarship for the relocated artist, plus insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and training, visa support, and personnel funding for the host organisation. No application fee.

Duration: Up to 15 months, starting no earlier than 15 January 2027

Deadline: 11 Sep 2026

The Martin Roth-Initiative is the German temporary-relocation programme for artists and cultural actors at risk, run jointly by the Goethe-Institut and ifa with Federal Foreign Office funding. Programme Line 1 relocates an artist to Germany for up to 15 months on a scholarship, with insurance, language courses, psychosocial support, counselling and visa assistance, plus personnel funding for the hosting organisation. ELIGIBILITY: artists and cultural practitioners anywhere in the world who are demonstrably committed through their work to an open society, freedom, peace and democracy; who face threats, persecution or unsafe living conditions; who have no access to a safe place to continue working; and who speak English or German. Applicants must still be active in their home country or have left it after 20 February 2026. Citizens of EU and EEA countries, Australia, Canada, Israel, New Zealand, Switzerland, the UK and the USA are excluded, as are residents of Gaza and previous MRI recipients. HOST REQUIREMENT: applications are submitted jointly with a non-profit host organisation in Germany (museum, theatre, festival, cultural collective, NGO) that is a legal entity able to handle the administrative and digital-security requirements. Note that the scholarship visa does not itself permit employment or self-employment in Germany. TIMELINE: applications 6 July to 11 September 2026; decisions end of November 2026; funding starts no earlier than 15 January 2027. Apply to apply@mri-application.de (encrypted email recommended); phone +49 30 284491-77.

item.title: ZMINA Resilience: Support for International Showcasing of Co-Creation Projects
item.description:
Organisation: IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA), Malý Berlín (SK), Trans Europe Halles (SE)

Location: Ukraine + Creative Europe partner countries

Award: Up to €50,000 per project (covers up to 90% of costs; remaining 10% must be a monetary own contribution); 19 to 25 grants from a €950,000 pot

Duration: Per showcasing project

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

Second strand of the ZMINA: Resilience project (run by IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK) with Trans Europe Halles (SE)), funding the international showcasing and public presentation of artistic works CO-CREATED by Ukrainian and other Creative Europe cultural organisations. Where the co-creation strand funds making the work, this strand funds bringing finished co-creations to wider audiences through showcasing and presentation events in Ukraine and across other Creative Europe countries. Projects are expected to adapt works to new audiences through active partner cooperation, for example by contextualising works, providing translation, involving local artists, experts and communities, and running parallel programmes. All creative and cultural sectors are eligible except audiovisual. ELIGIBILITY: organisations active in the arts and culture sectors, registered in a Creative Europe country (EU and non-EU); Ukrainian partners must be registered in territory under the effective control of the Ukrainian government. Proposals are submitted by a single lead applicant but the project must include at least two partner organisations from at least two countries, one of which is Ukraine, with a genuine balance of roles and value across partners. FUNDING: total pool €950,000; grants up to €50,000 covering up to 90% of project costs, with the remaining 10% provided by applicants as a monetary (not in-kind) own contribution; 19 to 25 grants expected. item.title: Stimuleringsfonds: Open Call Grounding the Cloud 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie (Creative Industries Fund NL)

Location: Netherlands. Requires Dutch Chamber of Commerce (KvK) registration within the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Award: Maximum EUR 30,000 per grant. No application fee.

Duration: Project-based; maximum project duration one year.

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

Open call from the Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds) for projects within digital culture that provide insight into and reduce the ecological impact of digital technology. Data storage in the cloud, generative AI chatbots and other everyday digital habits carry major ecological consequences: the energy consumption of data centres, the raw materials used for hardware, and ever-growing e-waste. The Fund encourages projects that make the ecological (and therefore also social) impact of digital technologies and data consumption tangible, question it, and put alternative working methods into practice, around topics such as regenerative culture, degrowth, low-tech, the reuse of obsolete hardware, and responsibility for the technologies we use within digital culture. Applications may concern new projects or the reinterpretation or further development of existing initiatives that show scope for more depth or a changed approach. Collaborations in which designers, makers or researchers engage with sustainability from an intersectional perspective are explicitly encouraged. The grant may be used for artistic and substantive development, research, collaboration, knowledge sharing, presentation and documentation. ELIGIBILITY: individual makers, designers, researchers or collectives working on alternative ways of handling digital technology, registered with a Chamber of Commerce within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Grant awards a maximum of EUR 30,000; maximum project duration one year. This call is open from 17 August 2026, 15:00 CEST until 14 September 2026, 16:00 CEST. No application fee. Questions: digitalecultuur@stimuleringsfonds.nl.

item.title: Kone Foundation: Annual Grant Call (2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Kone Foundation / Koneen Saatio (Finland)

Location: Finland. Work may be carried out abroad by Finnish citizens. Projects must have a connection to Finland.

Award: Artistic groups and organisations up to EUR 250,000; research groups typically EUR 200,000 to 500,000. Minimum project duration six months for individual applicants and one month for groups; maximum four consecutive years for the same project. No co-financing requirement stated. No application fee. No retroactive funding.

Duration: One month to four years; projects must start in January or later.

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Kone Foundation is Finland's major private funder for academic research in the humanities, social sciences and environmental sciences, for professional artistic work across all disciplines, and specifically for multidisciplinary projects combining scholarly and artistic approaches, which is where digital culture, media arts and artistic research proposals land. Individuals, working groups and legal entities with a Finnish business ID may apply, and artistic groups and organisations can receive up to EUR 250,000. The Finland connection is the binding constraint: a non-Finnish applicant needs a Finnish institutional affiliation, Finland residence, or the work must happen in Finland, though international collaborators can join a group freely once one member is a Finnish citizen or Finland-based. Psychology, theology, law, business studies without an interdisciplinary element, and medical research are not funded, nor are master's studies, continuing education, building renovation, standalone equipment purchases or hobby activity. The annual call runs 1 to 15 September each year, closing 15 September 2026 at 16:00 EEST, with decisions announced in November and December. TIMING: funding is never retroactive and projects must begin in January or later, so a September 2026 application funds work starting January 2027 at the earliest. FLAG: Kone frames its funding around artistic work and research projects rather than festival or event hosting as such, so an event-led application needs to be framed as an artistic or research project.

item.title: Trust me, I'm an AI/rtist: Open Call for Creative Interventions
item.description:
Organisation: Waag Futurelab (Horizon Europe project HAMLET)

Location: Europe. Engaging with a specific AI Enabler includes an on-site visit to its technology partner: CERTH (Greece), The Audience Agency (Warrington, UK), the Centre of Excellence for Research & Innovation (Cyprus), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (Greece), or CAUSA Creation (Austria). Final presentations September 2027.

Award: EUR 20,000 commission fee excluding VAT, inclusive of artist fee, travel, accommodation and production costs. Applicants must have a VAT number in Europe. No application fee.

Duration: January to September 2027, with final presentations in September 2027

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

Waag Futurelab invites artists, theatre makers, choreographers, dancers, game designers and other creative practitioners to engage directly with seven experimental generative AI Enablers being co-created with technologists and dance, theatre and gaming professionals. The call is an invitation into the development process: selected artists get access to the technologies, datasets, interfaces and assumptions that shape these systems while they are still being built. Rather than testing whether the systems work, artists are asked to interrogate why they work the way they do, who they are designed for, what forms of creativity they enable or constrain, and what assumptions about culture, intelligence, authorship, labour, bodies, audiences and society are embedded in them. Waag is looking for individuals and collectives willing to move beyond adoption into investigation, and welcomes proposals that are speculative, critical, poetic, provocative, humorous, performative, constructive or disruptive, including work that challenges, misuses, reimagines, hacks, subverts or plays with the tools, exposes hidden biases, questions environmental costs, or imagines alternative technological futures. The Alliance is composed of the Bodossaki Foundation, Fondation BNP Paribas, Fondation CHANEL, Fondazione con il Sud, Fondation de France, Fondation RAJA-Danièle Marcovici, King Baudouin Foundation and L'Oréal Fund for Women; this particular fund is backed by all of those except Fondation BNP Paribas. OBJECTIVE: to foster collaboration and solidarity within European intersectional and grassroots movements so that they can collectively advance gender equality in Europe in the long term. The call follows a 2025 Alliance-commissioned mapping of European gender-equality movements (30 in-depth interviews plus contextual research) which found movements under-resourced because philanthropic funding frameworks are misaligned with their needs; the fund is designed to replace short-term reactive funding with proactive long-term support. OUTCOMES SOUGHT: community organising reinforced at local or national level; pan-European feminist collaborations and solidarity strengthened; alliances between gender equality and other social justice movements expanded; pro-gender-equality narratives and voices amplified in local, national, regional or digital spaces; policy debates informed by feminist and gender equality movements. ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE (non-exhaustive): national, regional or pan-European convenings and collaborative projects where groups co-create joint strategies; joint campaigns between feminist movements and allied movements (climate justice, anti-racism, LGBTQI+, disability rights); narrative-change training for grassroots groups covering framing, messaging, digital tools and digital storytelling; cross-border coalitions advocating EU institutions or national governments; facilitated virtual or in-person convenings to work through internal tensions and build trust; translating academic research on anti-gender efforts into movement strategies. ELIGIBILITY: collective proposals with at least 3 organisations per coalition (no maximum); legally registered non-profits (NGOs, civil society organisations, social enterprises, national or regional funds); based and operating in the target countries; small and medium grassroots organisations, defined by annual budget under EUR 450,000 (Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Sweden, UK) or under EUR 300,000 (Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Republic of Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Serbia). Intermediary organisations and networks are exempt from the budget thresholds but must apply in coalition with grassroots organisations, with the budget fairly distributed among all partners. Coalitions must be community-led (majority of leadership roles held by members of the community supported, and/or participatory approaches), work with marginalised women, transgender, non-binary and gender non-conforming people, use gender transformative approaches, and hold an intersectional perspective. Proposals must be completed in English. Each organisation may submit only one application, as lead or as partner. One organisation per coalition acts as lead, is the primary contact and is legally responsible for the grant; leads are invited to networking, peer-learning and capacity-strengthening activities. SCORING (100 points): relevance to the call objective 20; demonstrated track record in strengthening movements 20 (learnings valued as well as achievements); strong impact 25 (must contribute to at least one of the five outcomes, with clear measurement); ability to work collaboratively and inclusively with partners 20 (including fair budget repartition); quality and feasibility 15. PROCESS: two stages. Stage 1 opened 29 June 2026 and closes 7 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST, submitted in English via the online platform (a PDF of the form is downloadable for reference only). Pre-selection results by email 14 September 2026; stage 2 runs 16 September to 23 October 2026 and includes due-diligence contact from Alliance staff; final results by email in December 2026; grants start January 2027. The Alliance is piloting a participatory selection process for this call, with grant-making decisions made jointly by a committee of funders and non-funders holding equal decision-making power. item.title: Onassis ONX & ACE: Summer School 2026, Innovation, Tech & Culture (Worldbuilding)
item.description:
Organisation: Onassis ONX, in collaboration with ACE (Athens Center for Entrepreneurship & Innovation, AUEB) and NYU Tandon School of Engineering

Location: Athens, Greece (Athens University of Economics and Business); in-person attendance required.

Award: Free educational program (NO participation fee and no application fee), not a paid grant: there is no stipend, and travel and accommodation are not mentioned as covered. BENEFITS: lectures and mentorship from internationally recognised artists, designers, entrepreneurs and tech professionals (AUEB, NYU Tandon, and Onassis ONX Fellows in Athens and New York); access to funding opportunities and an incubation program for selected teams after completion; exposure to cutting-edge digital tools and interdisciplinary collaboration; and networking. Limited to 30 participants.

Duration: Two weeks, 1 to 13 July 2026

Deadline: Closed 21 Jun 2026

The Summer School: Innovation, Tech & Culture, organised by Onassis ONX and ACE for a third consecutive year, invites creative professionals and teams to explore the convergence of art, technology and sustainable entrepreneurship, bridging Culture and Digital Arts with Technology, Artificial Intelligence and Entrepreneurship. The 2026 edition is again dedicated to 'Worldbuilding', a methodology that fuels innovation and fosters novel entrepreneurial models: the emphasis shifts from the project or end product to the narratives that frame and sustain them, building immersive worlds around products and turning the audience into co-shapers of the experience. The program challenges traditional product design and promotion practices by harnessing new technologies, art thinking and innovative design. SYLLABUS: Media & Art History; Speculative & Interactive Design Theory; Ethics, Art & Technology; Computational Creativity; AI-enabled Tech Development; Innovation & Entrepreneurship (business modeling and product validation); building for speed with venture capital backing; understanding the market and audience; branding, marketing and digital channels; and IP management, licensing and contracts. Participants attend lectures and receive mentorship from keynote speakers of AUEB, the NYU Tandon School of Engineering and Onassis ONX Fellows, plus talks by leading international professionals such as artist-technologists Jiabao Li and Cooper Galvin. OPPORTUNITIES: access to funding opportunities and an incubation program for selected teams after completion; development of entrepreneurial, artistic and technological skills; and networking and growth opportunities for participating companies. WHO CAN APPLY: undergraduate and postgraduate students and early-career professionals; established professionals and corporate employees in arts, culture, design, marketing, technology and business administration. PARTICIPATION: individual application, or as a member of a corporate team or company representative; in-person attendance required; working language English; up to 30 participants. item.title: OASIS: Disappearing Landscape Residency 2026 (High Tatras, Slovakia)
item.description:
Organisation: Association for Nature Conservation - Machaon International, with Kolaj 22 and Ukrainian-Slovak HUB (European OASIS project)

Location: High Tatras, Slovakia

Award: Artist fee up to EUR 1,300; travel support up to EUR 300 (for international artists); production/material support up to EUR 300; accommodation and meals; access to workspaces and partner venues; organisational support and networking; public presentation opportunities; excursions in the High Tatras region. No application fee.

Duration: 9-day international art residency, 14 to 22 August 2026

Deadline: Closed 07 Jun 2026

European OASIS project residency in the High Tatras, where artists, youth culture and alternative creative spaces unite to respond to the rapid loss of Carpathian landscapes, wildlife habitats and authentic mountain life. The High Tatras and surrounding Carpathian landscapes are rapidly changing under uncontrolled construction, expansion of tourism infrastructure, and fragmentation of natural habitats: forest ecosystems and wildlife migration corridors are disappearing, rivers drying up, and mountain landscapes increasingly transformed into commercial recreational zones. The Disappearing Landscape Art Residency explores how art and independent culture can reflect on and communicate the rapid degradation of the Carpathian landscape, connecting environmental awareness with youth culture, music and alternative artistic spaces, and reaching new audiences (especially young people often outside traditional institutional formats). DISCIPLINES: visual artists, musicians, filmmakers, photographers, interdisciplinary creators, and collectives or small creative teams whose projects address environmental change, disappearing landscapes, and the relationship between culture, community and activism. PROGRAMME SUPPORT: accommodation and meals; access to workspaces and partner venues; organisational support and networking; public presentation opportunities; excursions in the High Tatras region; travel support up to EUR 300 for international artists; production/material support up to EUR 300; artist fee up to EUR 1,300. transmediale 2027's Lattice Labs are experimental working groups dedicated to rethinking and testing alternatives to technological monocultures of extraction and surveillance, in preparation of the festival. Each Lab has roughly five participants guided by an experienced artist or technologist, structured around flat hierarchies and peer-to-peer learning, with the aim of producing prototypes, tools and projects that articulate shared languages to organise, resist and live otherwise. Programme blocks include online Collective Vocabulary Sessions (Block 1), a 3-day in-person design sprint in Berlin (Block 2, October 2026), online implementation and festival prep (Block 3, November-December 2026), a workshop/panel presentation at transmediale (Block 4, January 2027), and ongoing long-term organising afterwards (Block 5). WHO: early-career and emerging artists, researchers, curators, students and practitioners from any discipline (art and culture, design, tech, writing, publishing, academia, law, labour organising, etc.); transdisciplinary cohorts are sought. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be based in (and around) the EU. Only one application per candidate across all labs; no collective applications. item.title: MedSEA: Socially Engaged Arts in the Mediterranean - Open Call 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Larnaka 2030, Al Badil, Liv.in.g and Busart (Creative Europe consortium)

Location: Residencies in Larnaka (Cyprus) and Sfax (Tunisia); applicants must legally reside in a Creative Europe-eligible country

Award: Full support: travel, accommodation, artistic fee, mentorship and access to an international network of artists and cultural professionals.

Duration: Multi-phase programme October 2026 - May 2027: capacity-building phase plus a four-week residency (Larnaka 5 October - 1 November 2026; Sfax 5 April - 2 May 2027)

Deadline: Closed 05 Jun 2026

MedSEA (Socially Engaged Arts in the Mediterranean Area) is a Creative Europe cooperation project where artistic practices engage directly with communities, territories and the social transformations shaping the Mediterranean. This open call selects 12 emerging artists and cultural professionals working - or wishing to work - with participatory and socially engaged artistic practices. It is a process of co-creation in real contexts rather than a traditional residency: participants work directly with local communities developing territory-rooted artistic projects. The programme runs in phases - a preparation and capacity-building phase (webinars and workshops on community-based artistic practices, sustainability and cultural project design), then a four-week residency of fieldwork and co-creation supported by project partners. Residencies take place in Larnaka, Cyprus (5 October - 1 November 2026) and Sfax, Tunisia (5 April - 2 May 2027); resulting works are presented at the Mahallart Festival in Larnaka and the Hors-Lits Festival in Sfax. ELIGIBILITY: artists and cultural professionals aged 18 or above, legally residing in a country eligible under the Creative Europe Programme, and actively engaged in community-based or socially engaged artistic practices across disciplines such as visual arts, performing arts, interdisciplinary practices and public space interventions. Selected participants receive full support: travel, accommodation, artistic fee, mentorship and network access. Implemented by a consortium of Larnaka 2030 (Cyprus), Al Badil (Tunisia), Liv.in.g (Italy) and Busart (Greece); co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union. Deadline 5 June 2026, 23:59 CET. Contact: maria@larnaka2030.eu.
